cards.explanation: The answer is False. The text says she “…gave birth to a son.” (Exodus 2:2) Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had ordered that the Hebrew sons be thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1:22). So a baby boy was born right into the middle of that order.

The answer is True, friends. The text says “…she hid him for three months.” (Exodus 2:2) Three whole months. I couldn't keep a cookie box shut for three minutes, and she kept a baby tucked away that long.
The answer is a papyrus basket, friends. The text says she “…got him a papyrus basket…” (Exodus 2:3) Then she coated it with tar and pitch. That's one small basket doing a very big job.

The answer is reeds, friends. She set the basket “…among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.” (Exodus 2:3) Reeds are the tall plants that grow at the water's edge. She put the basket right in them, close to the bank.

The answer is to see what would happen to him. The text says his sister “…stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.” (Exodus 2:4) She was watching, and that's the reason the verse gives. I think she watched that basket like I watch the oven timer.

The answer is False, friends. Pharaoh's daughter, the daughter of Egypt's king, saw the basket and “…sent her maidservant to retrieve it.” (Exodus 2:5) She didn't walk past it. A basket in the reeds got her attention.

The answer is compassion, friends. The text says “…the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him…” (Exodus 2:6) A crying baby changed the whole moment for her. And she was the daughter of the very king who gave the order about the Hebrew sons (Exodus 1:22).

The answer is Hebrew, friends. She opens that basket, sees a crying little boy, and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) That's the word she used. And the verse says she had compassion on him. I think a crying baby got to her before anything else did.

The answer is to call a Hebrew woman to nurse him. The sister asked, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?” (Exodus 2:7) She had the whole idea ready. I just hope my own big ideas land as well as hers did.

The answer is the boy's mother, friends. The text says “…the girl went and called the boy’s mother.” (Exodus 2:8) Out of every woman she could have called, she called his own mother. I think that's a plot twist worth a gasp.

The answer is True, friends. Pharaoh's daughter said, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” (Exodus 2:9) A mother gets her own baby back and a paycheck on top of it. Now THAT is a good day at work.

The answer is that he becomes her son, friends. The text says, “…he became her son.” (Exodus 2:10) The boy was brought to Pharaoh's daughter after he had grown older. So a Hebrew baby ends up with a place in Pharaoh's own family.

The answer is water, friends. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) The name comes from that moment at the river. A basket in the reeds, and a boy pulled out of the Nile.
